headline: Microchip and Siemens report full-chip AMS verification for FPGA I/O PVT calibration
fact: At DAC 2026, Microchip and Siemens authors described full-chip analog mixed-signal verification of FPGA I/O PVT calibration spanning distributed I/O banks. The presented calibration combines a SAR-based digital block with analog circuitry that manages reference currents and voltages. The authors report that Siemens Symphony Pro reduced simulation time by about 3x and memory usage by about 2-3x while supporting regression across multiple I/O standards and extreme PVT conditions; these are presentation-reported results for the described case.

sources.title: An Optimized Full-Chip Analog Mixed-Signal (AMS) Verification Approach for PVT Calibration in FPGA Systems
sources.summary: The official DAC 2026 record identifies the Microchip and Siemens authors, July 28 presentation, SAR/digital-plus-analog PVT-calibration architecture, full-chip verification scope, and reported approximately-3x simulation-time and 2-3x memory improvements.
